learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of eight certificate submissions should be certified, revised and resubmitted, or declared not eligible, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** certificate-submission-reviewer
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight certificate submissions should be certified, revised and resubmitted, or declared not eligible, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Certificate, Certificate Requirements, Certificate Submission, Submission Review (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each submission the learner commits one of three outcomes. An outcome is correct when it matches the Correct outcome column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the five requirements is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Attendance and effort earn the certificate. (2) A submission with one gap is declined for good. (3) A claimed gain needs no checking. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a submission against the requirements is an Evaluate-level action. Submissions that meet all requirements, miss one that can be fixed, or miss one that cannot teach the learner to apply the standard evenly. **Content:** The three outcomes: Certify, Revise and resubmit, Not eligible. The five requirements, available on demand: attend the full day; complete the calibration exercise and explain each flagged metric; submit an evaluation on all 10 metrics with evidence and a note on every agent finding; publish an improved component under CC BY with metadata that gains on at least two quality and two reusability metrics; submit within 30 days. The eight submissions (all made up): | # | Submission | Correct outcome | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Complete worksheet with evidence for all 10 metrics and a findings log of 5 entries (3 accepted, 1 corrected, 1 rejected). The component is published under CC BY with metadata. Gains: Accessibility +3 and Practice +2 on quality, Modularity +3 and Metadata +4 on reusability. Submitted on day 28. | Certify | It meets every requirement. | | 2 | Gains on two quality metrics and one reusability metric. Everything else is complete. | Revise and resubmit | It needs a gain on a second reusability metric. | | 3 | The improved component is published under CC BY-NC. Everything else is complete. | Revise and resubmit | The requirement is a CC BY license. | | 4 | The findings log lists 6 agent findings, all marked accepted with no reasons. | Revise and resubmit | There is no sign that the agent's output was checked. | | 5 | Evidence is missing for 4 of the 10 scores. | Revise and resubmit | Each score needs evidence. | | 6 | The re-score claims that all five images now have alt text, and the published component shows two images with none. | Revise and resubmit | The claimed gain is not supported by the component. | | 7 | The teacher did not attend the training day and watched a recording. | Not eligible | Attendance cannot be made up by revision. | | 8 | Complete worksheet; the two flagged metrics are explained; gains on three quality and three reusability metrics; CC BY with metadata; submitted on day 21. | Certify | It meets every requirement. | **Provenance:** The submissions are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The requirements follow the sample rubric worksheet in the book's workshop section. **Rules:** Each submission has exactly one correct outcome. Two are Certify, five are Revise and resubmit, and one is Not eligible. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one submission and the three outcomes, and may open the five requirements. Opening them does not change the score. 2. The learner chooses an outcome, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After submission 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 submissions in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [outcome]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The outcome is [outcome]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can review a submission fairly." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed submission. **Starting State:** The first submission in the shuffled order and the three outcomes. The question shown is "What should the reviewer decide?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of five requirements and its five review steps are the basis of this sim.
